$comment: Rules for German medical documents. 'applies_to' is an ontology class id; a rule applies to that class and all its descendants (medical_document = every document). Patterns are Python regular expressions matched case-insensitively. output_pattern rules check the AI's own explanation, not the document.

rules.message: Discharge letters normally list the medicines to take at home, but none were extracted. Check the 'Medikation' section of the letter.
Doctor's letters normally state the diagnoses, but none were extracted. Check the 'Diagnose' section of the letter.
No follow-up appointment was extracted. Ask your family doctor when you should come back after the hospital stay.
This is a medication plan, but no medicines were extracted. Do not rely on this explanation; read the plan itself or ask your pharmacist.
The document mentions a medicine and dose ({fact}) that is not part of any extracted medicine. A medicine may be missing — check the document.
The document contains an intake schedule ({fact}) that is not part of any extracted medicine. Check the document.
The document says that a medicine ({fact}) was stopped, paused, started or changed, but it is not in the extracted medicines. Check the document.
The document mentions a follow-up appointment ({fact}) that is not listed among the important details.
The document names warning signs ({fact}) that are not listed among the important details.
The document lists a diagnosis code ({fact}) that is not explained among the important details.
The document gives an instruction (“{fact}”) that is not listed among the important details.
The document lists a phone number ({fact}) that is not shown among the important details.
Methotrexate for rheumatism or psoriasis is usually taken only ONCE A WEEK. Taking it every day by mistake is dangerous. Check the day on your plan and ask your pharmacist if you are unsure.
This is a blood thinner. Do not stop or change it on your own, tell every doctor and dentist that you take it, and watch for unusual bleeding.
Insulin doses must be followed exactly. Know the signs of low blood sugar (sweating, shaking, confusion) and always carry some sugar.
The explanation suggests stopping a medicine, but the document does not say so. Never stop a medicine without asking your doctor.
The explanation suggests changing a dose, but the document does not say so. Only your doctor can change a dose.

rules.pattern: nothing to worry about|no need to worry|no need to see a doctor|not serious|harmless|kein grund zur sorge|harmlos|nicht schlimm
rules.message: The explanation reassures you in a way the document does not. Only your doctor can judge how serious something is.

rules.reason: The document names warning signs ({fact}). If they occur: in an emergency call 112; outside practice hours call 116117.
You have a right to an explanation you can understand (§ 630e BGB) and to see your records (§ 630g BGB). Ask your doctor about anything that is unclear.
Questions about your medicines? Pharmacists explain them free of charge. Keep this plan with you and show it to every doctor.
